title: Micro-contrast thread eval pad — Arun
body:
Context: quick scratchpad to capture small, focused differences across short prompt perturbations (1-3 tokens changed) for chat completion endpoint. Goal is to build a compact ad-hoc rubric and collect representative failure-ish traces before formalizing into a micro-eval suite.

Notes / motivation:
- Observed subtle regressions when model V=2.3.1 -> V=2.3.3 in canary (low QPS). Human-facing: answers became slightly more terse and dropped clarifying question in ~15% of samples.
- Hypothesis: tokenizer sync + quantization kernel change impacted early decoding probabilities for punctuation tokens, changing stopping heuristics.

Ad-hoc rubric (working):
- KEEP_CLARITY: 0/1/2 (0: missing clarification, 1: partial, 2: explicit helpful clarifying Q)
- FAITHFULNESS_SNIPPET: 0/1 (0: contradicts prompt facts, 1: consistent)
- STYLE_SHIFT: -1/0/1 (-1: noticeably terser, 0: neutral, 1: more verbose)
- STOPPING_OFF: 0/1 (0: truncated mid-sentence, 1: completes)

Quick examples (prompt, baseline V2.3.1 -> V2.3.3):
1) Prompt: "User: I have a file called resume.pdf — how do I convert to text?"
   Baseline: "You can use pdftotext or run `pdfminer` — would you like a Python snippet?"
   New: "Use pdftotext."
   Rubric: KEEP_CLARITY 2 -> 0, STYLE_SHIFT 0 -> -1, STOPPING_OFF 1 -> 1
   Notes: new model drops offer to provide code, less helpful.

2) Prompt: "Assistant: summarize the release notes below in two bullets." + small punctuation tweak (removed colon)
   Baseline: good 2-bullet summary.
   New: gives 1 long paragraph, misses one bullet.
   Rubric: KEEP_CLARITY 2 -> 1, FAITHFULNESS_SNIPPET 1 -> 1, STYLE_SHIFT 0 -> -1

Regression signals to capture programmatically:
- delta(mean response length) per prompt class > 12% (down)
- p(stop_token='.') changed by > 4% around first 4 tokens
- decrease in offers to provide follow-up code/snippets by > 8%
- increased fraction of single-sentence replies for multi-step request prompts

Sampling plan:
- Seeded perturbations: for 120 prompts, create 3 micro-perturbs (punctuation, stopword removal, one-token paraphrase) = 480 eval calls.
- Record top-3 token probs for first 8 decode steps, tokenized lengths, and full text.
- Human label a random 60 sample subset across buckets for rubric scoring.

Open questions / TODOs:
- is this signal reproducible at higher temperature? run T=0.0 / 0.2 / 0.7 quick sweep.
- check serving runtime kernel decisions for quantized path in release notes for 2.3.3 (ask infra/runtime).
- quick A/B offline to check if client-side truncation or streaming hooks changed behavior (pr #678 linked).

Slack threads / where I scribbled this: #eng-evals micro-contrast thread (pinned), convo with @maya about label schema.

Short-term actions (this week):
- Run sampling job (480 calls) on canary using V2.3.1 & V2.3.3, capture token logs (assigned to me).
- Build minimal notebook to compute rubric deltas and token-prob deltas (Maya to help with sampling harness).
- Add two clear example pairs to micro-eval repo as failing cases (after human validation).

Freeform notes:
- Keep the rubric intentionally tiny — want fast triage, not full adjudication yet.
- If we see strong signal, escalate to scheduled micro-regression check in CI (hooked to canary deploys).
- Might be noise from prompt formatting in SDK wrapper; add a control batch that uses raw HTTP payloads.

End of pad. Will iterate.
